Updated read-through using SLOOS as a cross-check:

- Policy: FOMC held 5.25–5.50% and kept QT caps unchanged ($60B UST, $35B MBS), with IORB at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%, and ON repo min 5.5%. Guidance remains data dependent and explicitly mindful of cumulative tightening and policy lags.
- SLOOS lens: Banks report broad-based tightening in credit supply across categories:
  - Business credit: C&I and CRE standards tighter at large and foreign banks, with tighter covenants and wider loan rate spreads; reasons cited include higher funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, and declines in the market value of fixed‑income assets. Foreign banks also highlight collateral values and ease of selling loans.
  - Household credit: Terms tightened further for credit card and auto loans; banks indicate a greater emphasis on FICO/approval likelihood and wider spreads/fees. Residential mortgage categories remain tight across QM/non‑QM segments and HELOCs.
  - While some banks note credit quality/economic outlook as reasons for limited easing in select pockets, the net stance remains restrictive.
- Implications: SLOOS corroborates the FOMC’s statement that tighter financial and credit conditions will weigh on activity and inflation. Together with FSR-flagged vulnerabilities (CRE refinancing pressures, NBFI fragilities, funding-cost sensitivity), the near-term growth tilt is modestly more negative than a macro-only read, while disinflation credibility is reinforced.

Net assessment: Restrictive policy is maintained; SLOOS shows ongoing contraction in credit availability to businesses and households, increasing downside growth risks. Adjusting for SLOOS, the balance of risks tilts more negative than previously indicated.
